answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a stake that is slashable when an identity is proven to have double-voted or violated a signed rule. A newcomer posts collateral before joining consensus; the protocol then randomly audits a small sample of actions, and a valid fraud proof burns that identity’s stake. Spawning a thousand aliases no longer gives free influence: each must lock capital, while audits make coordinated cheating risk losing it. The gale of fake accounts meets an oasis only if the attacker can afford the cedar-sized collateral bill.
